title: Music
about: Collocations for talking about music: describing songs, albums and performances (a catchy tune, a massive hit, a live performance), the music business (release an album, go on tour, go solo) and playing an instrument yourself (take up the guitar, tune an instrument).

items.pattern: the (rock / jazz / local) music scene · arrive on / burst onto the scene · noun + noun
items.meaning: the world of a particular kind of music in a place: the bands, the clubs, the fans and everything that is happening there
items.example: My brother moved to Berlin because he wanted to be part of its electronic **music scene**.
more: Ten years ago nobody had heard of them; now they're the biggest names on the indie **music scene**.
When I was a student, the local **music scene** was mostly cover bands playing in pubs.
items.watchOut: Music scene — не сцена, на якій грають (це stage: go on stage), а музичне життя: гурти, клуби, фанати. Новий гурт «з'являється на сцені» — arrives on / bursts onto the music scene.

items.pattern: (soft / quiet) background music · put on / play some background music · noun + noun
items.meaning: quiet music that plays while you are doing something else and not really listening to it
items.example: The restaurant had soft **background music**, so we could chat without shouting.
more: I can't work in silence, so I keep some **background music** on all day.
The **background music** at the dentist's was meant to relax me, but it didn't.
items.watchOut: Music — незлічуване: some background music, а не a background music чи musics. А фоновий шум — background noise.

items.pattern: music blasts out (from / of sth) · blast out music · be blasting out · verb + adverb
items.meaning: (of music) play extremely loudly
items.example: Music was **blasting out** of the flat upstairs until three in the morning.
more: My teenage son likes to **blast out** heavy metal while he does his homework.
During the football match, music was **blasting out** from every bar in the square.
items.watchOut: Після blast out — from або of: blasting out of the car. Blast — це завжди дуже гучно; про музику, що грає тихо, кажуть is playing quietly / softly.

items.pattern: a debut album / single / concert · make your debut · noun used like an adjective + noun
items.meaning: the first album that a singer or band makes and presents to the public
items.example: The band recorded their **debut album** in a friend's garage in two weeks.
more: Her **debut single** came out when she was still at school.
The young pianist will make her **debut** with the city orchestra next month.
items.watchOut: Вимова: /ˈdeɪbjuː/ — t у кінці не читається, у британській наголос на першому складі. Debut — і іменник (her debut), і означення перед іменником (a debut album).

items.pattern: a live performance / concert / recording · perform live · adjective + noun
items.meaning: a performance given in front of an audience, not recorded in a studio
items.example: Nothing beats the energy of a **live performance**: the crowd, the lights, the noise.
more: Their **live performances** are much better than their studio albums.
We watched a **live performance** of the opera on a big screen in the park.
items.watchOut: Прикметник live читається /laɪv/ (як five), а дієслово live — /lɪv/. «Живий виступ» — live performance, не living performance: living — про те, що живе (living things), а alive стоїть тільки після дієслова (He's alive).

items.pattern: easy listening · easy-listening music / station · noun, no article
items.meaning: light, relaxing music that is not serious or difficult to listen to
items.example: My parents always have an **easy-listening** station on in the car.
more: The hotel bar plays **easy listening** all evening, mostly soft piano.
Some people call it boring, but I like **easy listening** after a stressful day.
items.watchOut: Легка музика — easy listening (або light music), зазвичай не easy music. Це назва стилю, тож без артикля: I like easy listening.

items.pattern: a catchy tune / song / chorus / melody · adjective + noun
items.meaning: pleasant and easy to remember, so it quickly gets stuck in your head
items.example: That song has a **catchy tune**, but the words are a bit silly.
more: Football fans love a **catchy chorus** they can all sing together.
My dad made up a **catchy** little **tune** for my sister's birthday.
items.watchOut: «Прилипливий мотив» — catchy tune, зазвичай не sticky tune і не catching tune: catching — про хворобу (Is it catching? — Це заразно?).

items.pattern: give a (great / moving / sentimental) performance (of sth) · verb + noun
items.meaning: perform a piece of music, a play, etc. for an audience in a particular way
items.example: The jazz trio **gave a relaxed performance** in the hotel garden.
more: Grandad **gave** a rather sentimental **performance** of his favourite love song at the party.
Despite her nerves, my daughter **gave a confident performance** at her piano exam.
items.watchOut: «Виступити» — give a performance (або give a concert); make a performance у цьому значенні не кажуть. «Виконання» — performance, а не execution: execution — страта або виконання наказу.

items.pattern: a pop idol · a teen idol · sb's idol · noun + noun
items.meaning: a pop singer or musician who is a very big star and is loved by many, often young, fans
items.example: When I was thirteen, my bedroom walls were covered with posters of my favourite **pop idol**.
more: He went from singing in his uncle's restaurant to **pop idol** in less than a year.
My mum still screams when she hears her old **teen idol** on the radio.
items.watchOut: Idol читається /ˈaɪdl/ — так само, як idle (ледачий): перший звук «ай», а не «і», а о не вимовляється.

items.pattern: adoring fans / crowds / audience · adjective + noun
items.meaning: fans who love a star very much and admire everything they do
items.example: The singer stopped to take selfies with her **adoring fans** outside the theatre.
more: The band signed autographs for an hour for their **adoring fans**.
My little sister and her friends are **adoring fans** of a boy band from Korea.
items.watchOut: Фанати, що обожнюють, — adoring fans (-ing: це вони обожнюють). Adored — навпаки, «обожнюваний»: an adored singer.

items.pattern: a piece of music · a (short / beautiful) piece · a piece by Mozart · noun + of + noun
items.meaning: one musical work, e.g. a song or something written for an instrument or an orchestra
items.example: We chose a slow **piece of music** for our first dance at the wedding.
more: My grandad can hear a **piece of music** once and then play it on the piano.
The film ends with a beautiful **piece** for cello and piano.
items.watchOut: Music незлічуване: не a music і не musics, а a piece of music / pieces of music. Твір без слів — краще a piece, а не a song: song — тільки те, що співають.

items.pattern: a big / massive / huge hit · have a hit with sth · ↔ a minor hit · adjective + noun
items.meaning: a song or album that is extremely successful and very popular
items.example: My dad's favourite band had one **big hit** in 1985 and then disappeared.
more: The musical was a **massive hit** in London, so now it's moving to New York.
Not every song can be a **big hit**: most of their songs are known only to real fans.
items.watchOut: «Великий хіт» — a big / massive / huge hit, не a strong hit чи a heavy hit. «Мати хіт» — have a hit (with a song).

items.pattern: release an album / a single / a song · be released · a new release · verb + noun
items.meaning: make a new recording available for people to buy or listen to
items.example: The singer **released** her first album when she was only seventeen.
more: The band **released** a Christmas song to raise money for a children's hospital.
Most bands now **release** their songs online before the CD comes out.
items.watchOut: Альбом випускають — release, а не publish: publish — про книжки, газети, статті. Release ще означає «звільнити, відпустити», але про музику й фільми — «випустити».

items.pattern: write / compose music (for sth) · compose a piece / a symphony · a composer · verb + noun
items.meaning: create music; compose sounds more formal and is used especially for classical music
items.example: My cousin **writes music** for TV adverts and radio jingles.
more: She **composed** a short piece for her grandmother's funeral.
Who **wrote the music** for this film? It's beautiful.
items.watchOut: «Складати музику» — compose, не compile: compile — укладати збірку чи список. Compose звучить офіційніше, особливо про класичну музику; у розмові частіше write music. Make music теж кажуть, але ширше: створювати або грати музику (We make music together on Fridays).

items.pattern: a huge / large / loyal following · have / build up a following · ↔ a small following · adjective + noun
items.meaning: a very large group of fans who like a singer or band and follow what they do
items.example: Even after twenty years, the band still has a **huge following** and sells out every concert.
more: She started singing in local pubs and soon had a **loyal following** in the town.
The radio DJ has a **huge following** among taxi drivers.
items.watchOut: Following тут — іменник: «прихильники, фанати». Кажуть have a huge following, а не have huge followers: followers — частіше про соцмережі (two million followers).

items.pattern: go on tour · be on tour · a world / European tour · verb + on + noun
items.meaning: travel from place to place to give a series of concerts
items.example: Our neighbour's son plays drums in a band, and they're **going on tour** in Scotland this summer.
more: The singer is **on tour** for six months, so her kids travel with her.
We saw them in Lisbon during their **world tour**.
items.watchOut: «Поїхати на гастролі» — go on tour (без артикля), не make a tour. «Бути на гастролях» — be on tour.

items.pattern: a haunting melody / tune / song / voice · adjective + noun
items.meaning: beautiful and usually a little sad, so you keep remembering it for a long time
items.example: The film opens with a **haunting melody** played on a single violin.
more: I still remember the **haunting** song my grandmother sang to us at bedtime.
The church bells played a **haunting tune** that echoed across the valley.
items.watchOut: Haunting — не «моторошний» і не «з привидами» (це haunted: a haunted house). A haunting melody — гарна й трохи сумна мелодія, яку довго не можеш забути.

items.pattern: a virtuoso performance · the occasional virtuoso performance · a virtuoso pianist / violinist · a virtuoso (noun) · noun used like an adjective + noun
items.meaning: a performance that shows extremely great skill
items.example: The young cellist gave a **virtuoso performance**, and the whole hall stood up to clap.
more: You don't need to be a **virtuoso** to enjoy playing the piano.
The festival ended with a **virtuoso** violinist playing fast folk dances.
items.watchOut: Virtuoso — і іменник (віртуоз), і означення перед іменником: a virtuoso performance. Не плутай з virtuous — доброчесний.

items.pattern: capture / reach / attract a wider (bigger, younger) audience · verb + adjective + noun
items.meaning: succeed in getting more people, or new kinds of people, to listen to or enjoy something
items.example: The singer started writing songs in English to **capture a wider audience** abroad.
more: Free concerts in the park help the orchestra **reach a wider audience**.
The jazz club now has student nights to **attract a younger audience**.
items.watchOut: Аудиторію «завойовують» — capture / reach / attract an audience, не control. «Охопити аудиторію» — найчастіше reach an audience.

items.pattern: (a country's / rich) musical heritage · cultural / national heritage · adjective + noun
items.meaning: the music and musical traditions that a country or region has had for a long time
items.example: The festival celebrates the island's **musical heritage**, from fishermen's songs to brass bands.
more: Ireland is very proud of its rich **musical heritage**.
The old songs are part of our family's **musical heritage**: Grandma learned them from her grandmother.
items.watchOut: Спадщина країни, народу — heritage, а не inheritance: inheritance — спадок (гроші, будинок), який отримують після смерті родича.

items.pattern: conduct an orchestra / a choir / a band · a conductor · verb + noun
items.meaning: stand in front of a group of musicians and direct how they play or sing
items.example: She dreams of **conducting a big orchestra** in a famous concert hall one day.
more: Who's **conducting** the choir at the Christmas concert this year?
The **conductor** stopped the orchestra three times during the rehearsal.
items.watchOut: Диригент — conductor (слова dirigent англійською немає); у британському автобусі conductor — ще й кондуктор. «Диригувати оркестром» — conduct an orchestra, без прийменника.

items.pattern: a (classical / jazz) music lover · a lover of music · noun + noun
items.meaning: someone who enjoys music very much
items.example: My dad is a real **music lover**: he has more than two thousand records.
more: This shop is heaven for **jazz lovers**: shelves and shelves of old vinyl.
**Music lovers** from all over the world come to Vienna for the New Year concert.
items.watchOut: Меломан — music lover. Слова meloman англійською немає, melomaniac майже не кажуть, а music liker — не кажуть зовсім.

items.pattern: an album / a song / a concert features sb · featuring (feat.) sb · verb + noun
items.meaning: include someone or something as an important part, e.g. a guest singer on a song
items.example: The new song **features** a rapper from Brazil in the second verse.
more: The concert will **feature** a children's choir from a local school.
My favourite track on the album is the one **featuring** her dad on the piano.
items.watchOut: «За участю» — featuring (на обкладинках feat.). Не comprise: comprise — складатися з (The band comprises four musicians).

items.pattern: a rap artist / a rapper · rap music · a hip-hop artist · noun + noun
items.meaning: a performer who speaks rhymed words quickly over a strong beat
items.example: My nephew wants to be a **rap artist** and writes rhymes in the back of all his school books.
more: The festival has rock bands on Saturday and **rap artists** on Sunday.
The **rapper** wrote all the lyrics about growing up in his part of town.
items.watchOut: Реп «читають», але англійською rap — дієслово: He raps in English, а не reads rap. Artist у музиці — виконавець, не лише художник: a rap artist, a solo artist.

items.pattern: go solo · a solo artist / career / album · verb + adjective
items.meaning: leave a band and start performing alone
items.uk: почати сольну кар'єру, піти в сольне плавання
items.example: The drummer got tired of arguing with the others and **went solo**.
more: After ten years in a girl band, she **went solo** and had her first hit at thirty.
Lots of singers **go solo**, but few are as successful as they were in the band.
items.watchOut: «Почати сольну кар'єру» — go solo (go – went – gone), не get solo, become solo чи make solo.

items.pattern: remix a track / a song · a remix (of sth) · verb + noun
items.meaning: make a new version of a recorded song, often faster and for dancing
items.example: My brother **remixes** his favourite songs at weekends and plays them at parties.
more: Someone **remixed** my grandmother's favourite folk song, and now teenagers dance to it.
The new **remix** is twice as fast as the original.

items.pattern: an up-tempo number / song / track · ↔ a slow number · adjective + noun
items.meaning: a fast, lively song; number here means a song or piece in a show or on an album
items.example: The band finished the night with three **up-tempo numbers**, and everyone was dancing.
more: I always run faster when an **up-tempo** song comes on.
Her best **number** is a sad song about leaving home.
items.watchOut: Number тут — не «номер» у списку, а пісня чи музичний твір у програмі: a slow number. Tempo читається /ˈtempəʊ/.

items.pattern: strum a guitar / the strings / a few chords · verb + noun
items.meaning: play a guitar by moving your fingers or a pick across all the strings, often in a relaxed way
items.example: Someone was **strumming a guitar** by the campfire while the rest of us sang.
more: My daughter can only **strum** three chords, but she plays them every evening.
He sat on the back step, **strumming** quietly and humming to himself.
items.watchOut: «Грати на гітарі» — play the guitar (у британській зазвичай з the і без on). Strum — водити пальцями по всіх струнах, «бренькати»; смикати одну струну — pluck.

items.pattern: (have / show) musical talent · a talent for music · musically talented · adjective + noun
items.meaning: a natural ability to play, sing or write music well
items.example: She showed **musical talent** very early: at three she was picking out tunes on the piano.
more: You don't need any **musical talent** to enjoy karaoke!
My grandfather had great **musical talent**, but he never had the money for lessons.
items.watchOut: «Музичний слух» — an ear for music, а «музичний талант» — musical talent. Перед talent, instrument, family зазвичай ставлять прикметник musical (a musical instrument), хоча music lover, music scene — з іменником music.

items.pattern: take up the guitar / the piano / singing · take up a hobby · phrasal verb + noun
items.meaning: start learning to play an instrument or start a new activity
items.uk: почати вчитися грати на гітарі, взятися за гітару
items.example: My dad **took up the drums** at fifty, and the neighbours aren't happy.
more: I've **taken up the ukulele**: it's small enough to take on holiday.
After she retired, my aunt **took up** singing in a choir.
items.watchOut: Почати вчитися на інструменті — take up the guitar / the piano. Без up (take the guitar) — це просто «взяти гітару в руки».

items.pattern: live music · a live band / gig · play live · adjective + noun
items.meaning: music played by musicians in front of you, not a recording
items.example: I love **live music**: there's nothing like hearing a band right in front of you.
more: We hired a **live band** for our wedding instead of a DJ.
The café near the station has **live jazz** on Sunday afternoons.
items.watchOut: Live тут читається /laɪv/ (як five). «Жива музика» — live music, не alive music і не living music.

items.pattern: tune an instrument / a guitar / a piano · be in tune / out of tune · verb + noun
items.meaning: adjust the strings or other parts of an instrument so that it plays the right notes
items.example: It takes my brother ten minutes to **tune his guitar** before every lesson.
more: The old piano at school hasn't been **tuned** for years.
The choir sounded lovely, but one man was singing **out of tune**.
items.watchOut: «Налаштувати інструмент» — tune, не adjust і не set up. «Розладнаний» — out of tune; так само кажуть про людину, що фальшивить: sing out of tune.

items.pattern: play a piece (of music) · play a piece by Bach / for sb · verb + noun
items.meaning: perform a particular piece of music on an instrument
items.example: Could you **play a piece** for us? Anything you like!
more: My son is learning to **play a piece** by Bach for his piano exam.
She **played a lovely piece** by Debussy at her sister's wedding.
items.watchOut: «Зіграти п'єсу» на інструменті — play a piece (of music). A play — це п'єса в театрі (a play by Shakespeare).

warmup.q: The band have ___ a new album.
warmup.explain: Альбом випускають — release. Publish — про книжки й статті.

warmup.uk: Соліст пішов з гурту й почав сольну кар'єру.
warmup.q: The lead singer left the band and ___ solo.
warmup.explain: Почати сольну кар'єру — go solo (минулий час — went solo).

warmup.uk: Наступного літа вони поїдуть на гастролі до Італії.
warmup.q: Next summer they'll ___ on tour in Italy.
warmup.explain: Поїхати на гастролі — go on tour, без артикля.

warmup.uk: У суботу в барі буде жива музика.
warmup.q: There's ___ music at the bar on Saturday.

warmup.uk: У цієї пісні дуже прилипливий мотив.
warmup.q: This song has a really ___ tune.
warmup.explain: Мелодія, що чіпляє, — a catchy tune. Catching — заразний (про хворобу).
Меломан — music lover. Слова meloman англійською немає, а music liker не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Мій брат почав учитися грати на гітарі.
warmup.explain: Почати вчитися на інструменті — take up. Take the guitar — просто взяти гітару, take on — взяти на себе (роботу).

warmup.uk: Ми пишаємося музичною спадщиною нашого краю.
warmup.q: We're proud of our region's musical ___.
warmup.explain: Спадщина краю — heritage. Inheritance — спадок від родича, heirloom — родинна реліквія.

A.q: The ___ sound of the bagpipes across the empty hills stayed with me for days.
A.explain: Haunting — щемливий, незабутній. Haunted — з привидами (a haunted house), hunting — полювання.

A.q: The album ___ the singer's mother on two of the songs.
A.explain: Feature sb — мати когось серед учасників, «за участю». Comprise — складатися з (усіх частин), про гостя-виконавця так не кажуть; consist потребує of.

A.q: The band are huge in Japan, where they have a massive ___.
A.explain: Have a massive / huge following — мати величезну кількість шанувальників. Після a — однина: following.

B.q: A good musician can ___ a guitar just by listening.
B.explain: Налаштувати інструмент — tune. Set і tone тут не підходять.

B.q: My son has just ___ the trumpet, so it's very noisy at home.
B.explain: Take up an instrument — почати вчитися на ньому грати. Take on — взяти на себе (роботу), take over — перебрати контроль.

B.q: She's got real ___ talent: she can play any song after hearing it once.
B.explain: Перед talent — прикметник musical. Musician — музикант, musically — прислівник.

example.title: My sister's big plans
example.uk:
Минулого літа моя сестра почала вчитися грати на гітарі. У неї справжній музичний талант, і через два місяці вона вже могла зіграти родині коротку п'єсу. Потім її улюблений гурт оголосив, що їде на гастролі, і ми купили квитки.

Концерт був неймовірний. У гурту величезна кількість шанувальників, і стадіон був повний фанатів, які їх обожнюють. Вони почали з трьох швидких пісень, потім зіграли свій великий хіт десятирічної давності, і всі підспівували під його прилипливий мотив. Живий виступ гурту був набагато кращий за альбом.

Того вечора вдома сестра тихенько бренькала на гітарі у своїй кімнаті. Каже, що колись хоче почати сольну кар'єру. Щоправда, спершу їй потрібен гурт, з якого можна піти!

Last summer my sister [[took up the guitar|b3]]. She has real [[musical talent|b2]], and after two months she could [[play a short piece|b6]] for the family. Then her favourite band announced they were [[going on tour|a16]], so we bought tickets.

The concert was amazing. The band have a [[huge following|a15]], and the stadium was full of [[adoring fans|a10]]. They opened with three [[up-tempo numbers|a27]], then played their [[massive hit|a12]] from ten years ago, and everyone sang along to its [[catchy tune|a7]]. Their [[live performance|a5]] was much better than the album.

That night at home, my sister was quietly [[strumming|b1]] her guitar in her room. She says she wants to [[go solo|a25]] one day. First, though, she needs a band to leave!
